newsitem.title: USA: Koch pipeline blast sees minimal impact on butane.
newsitem.headline: Koch pipeline blast sees minimal impact on butane.

text.p: A deadly explosion Saturday at Koch Oil's Sterling pipeline system in the Gulf Coast has only minimally impacted distribution of natural gas liquids, a Koch spokesman said Monday.
"Impact from the pipeline explosion is minimal," corporate communications director Riff Yeager said.
He added "our larger line is still in service and we can still increase delivery on that line."
It remains unclear when flows on the 35,000 barrel per day (bpd) capacity pipeline would resume, he said.
The pipeline carrying normal butane exploded on Saturday apparently because of a leak that was ignited by a spark from a car being started, police said.
The explosion, in Lively, Texas, 40 miles southeast of Dallas, killed two teen-agers and forced 50 families to evacuate their homes.
The pipeline is the smaller of two in the Sterling system that feeds industrial customers in the Gulf Coast from storage facilities in Mont Belvieu, Texas.
The larger line has a 100,000 bpd capacity.
